sentences.text: do you know someone who is starting to learn english? we have a new easy video series just for them, the london letter challenge three teams race around london to find eight letters which will take them to the winning crowns.

sentences.speaker: 片头片尾
sentences.text: Watch the series on our website now: BBC Learning English dot com.

sentences.speaker: 片头片尾
sentences.text: Six minutes English from BBC Learning English dot com.

sentences.speaker: Neil
sentences.text: Hello, this is six Minute English from BBC Learning English.

sentences.speaker: Neil
sentences.text: I'm Neil.

sentences.speaker: Beth
sentences.text: And I'm Beth.

sentences.speaker: Neil
sentences.text: One area of technology which has been in the news a lot recently is robotics, the design and building of robots.

sentences.speaker: Neil
sentences.text: Humanoid robots, meaning robots which appear and behave like humans, are being built to help us do everything from washing the dishes to babysitting the kids.

sentences.speaker: Beth
sentences.text: But not everyone feels comfortable with the idea of inviting a human-like robot into their home.

sentences.speaker: Beth
sentences.text: Neil, how would you feel about living with a robot?

sentences.speaker: Neil
sentences.text: I really don't want to live with a robot.

sentences.speaker: Neil
sentences.text: I have enough people in my house.

sentences.speaker: Beth
sentences.text: With advances in AI, robots are becoming smart enough to develop meaningful relationships with humans.

sentences.speaker: Beth
sentences.text: There are reports of people telling their secrets to robot therapists and even falling in love with their robot friend.

sentences.speaker: Beth
sentences.text: In this episode, we'll meet a home companion robot called abby, who's making friends with the elderly residents of Melbourne in Australia.

sentences.speaker: Beth
sentences.text: And as usual, we'll learn some useful new vocabulary, all of which you 'll find over on our website, bbc learning english com.

sentences.speaker: Neil
sentences.text: First, I have a question for you, Beth.

sentences.speaker: Neil
sentences.text: Because it's important people feel safe around robots, engineers design them to look like the friendly characters seen in animated movies by studios like Pixar and DreamWorks.

sentences.speaker: Neil
sentences.text: So, what is the name of Pixar's friendly robot who picks up garbage on an uninhabited planet Earth in the year 2805?

sentences.speaker: Neil
sentences.text: Is it a), Roz?  b), wally, or c), R2D2?

sentences.speaker: Beth
sentences.text: I am pretty certain that the answer is b), wally.

sentences.speaker: Neil
sentences.text: Well, we'll find out the answer later in the program.

sentences.speaker: Neil
sentences.text: For five months during the Covid pandemic, Australian engineer Grace Brown had no human contact.

sentences.speaker: Neil
sentences.text: She used this time to build a home companion robot, abby, with the idea it would provide companionship to other people suffering loneliness.

sentences.speaker: Neil
sentences.text: Now Grace runs her own company Andromeda building robots specially designed as company for elderly residents in care homes who don't get many visitors Here she explains more about abby to BBC World Service program, The Conversation.

sentences.speaker: Neil
sentences.text: Abby, who's the humanoid robot that we build at Andromeda, people don't expect humanoid robots to have like so much personality.

sentences.speaker: Neil
sentences.text: She's very, very sassy.

sentences.speaker: Neil
sentences.text: She's very inquisitive and curious.

sentences.speaker: Neil
sentences.text: And I think when people meet her, they're always kind of taken back by…, "Oh, she's like got a mind of her own.".

sentences.speaker: Beth
sentences.text: When people meet Abby, they are surprised by her sassy personality.

sentences.speaker: Beth
sentences.text: The adjective sassy means bold, confident, and cheeky.

sentences.speaker: Neil
sentences.text: Some people are taken aback, meaning they are shocked or surprised by the things Abby says.

sentences.speaker: Neil
sentences.text: She really seems to be interested and to take care of the people she meets.

sentences.speaker: Neil
sentences.text: Abby can also express opinions, and Grace says she has a mind of her own, a phrase used when a non living object like a robot seems to be behaving or acting independently of human control.

sentences.speaker: Beth
sentences.text: Unlike the unpredictable and violent robots which are sometimes portrayed in sci fi movies abby is much more approachable and friendly, even funny she can blow bubbles from her hand.

sentences.speaker: Beth
sentences.text: Her softer design was a conscious decision by Grace, who wanted children and elderly people to interact with abby naturally and without fear, as she explained to BBC World services, The Conversation.

sentences.speaker: Beth
sentences.text: I originally modelled her off the size of like a young child, so like a six, seven- year-old child, so she's about 110 centimetres tall.

sentences.speaker: Beth
sentences.text: She's got a whole splash of different colours.

sentences.speaker: Beth
sentences.text: She's got, you know, large expressive eyes.

sentences.speaker: Beth
sentences.text: So that was, I was very much trying to replicate the kind of approachableness and the endearingness of like these different like Pixar characters that you'd watch in all of these films.

sentences.speaker: Beth
sentences.text: Abby

sentences.speaker: Neil
sentences.text: looks like a friendly character from a Pixar film.

sentences.speaker: Neil
sentences.text: She's the size of a six or seven year old child and decorated with a splash of color, a phrase used when a bit of color is added to brighten up something which is dull or unexciting.

sentences.speaker: Neil
sentences.text: Abby

sentences.speaker: Beth
sentences.text: also has large expressive eyes.

sentences.speaker: Beth
sentences.text: If you describe something as expressive, you mean it shows what someone thinks or feels.

sentences.speaker: Neil
sentences.text: Elderly residents who regularly chat with Abby say the robot companion brings them joy and a sense of community.

sentences.speaker: Beth
sentences.text: Ah, well, it is good to hear the positive side of technology, which can still seem a bit strange or frightening.

sentences.speaker: Beth
sentences.text: And I would like to see Abby blowing bubbles from her hand.

sentences.speaker: Beth
sentences.text: Now, isn't it time you revealed the answer to your question, Neil?

sentences.speaker: Neil
sentences.text: I asked you for the name of Pixar's friendly robot who picks up garbage on an uninhabited planet Earth in the year 2805.

sentences.speaker: Beth
sentences.text: And I said it was wally.

sentences.speaker: Neil
sentences.text: And you were… correct.

sentences.speaker: Beth
sentences.text: Yes.

sentences.speaker: Neil
sentences.text: That is the right answer okay, Let's recap the vocabulary we've learned, starting with humanoid, an adjective meaning to have the appearance and behavior of a human.

sentences.speaker: Beth
sentences.text: Someone who is sassy is bold, confident, and cheeky.

sentences.speaker: Neil
sentences.text: If you are taken aback by something, you are shocked or surprised by it.

sentences.speaker: Beth
sentences.text: If you say an object has a mind of its own, you mean that it seems to be acting independently without human control.

sentences.speaker: Neil
sentences.text: The phrase a splash of color is used when a bit of color is added to brighten something which is dull or unexciting.

sentences.speaker: Beth
sentences.text: And finally, the adjective expressive means showing what someone thinks or feels.

sentences.speaker: Beth
sentences.text: Once again, our six minutes are up.

sentences.speaker: Beth
sentences.text: If you've enjoyed this episode, then head over to our website BBC Learning English dot com, where you'll find a quiz and worksheet to practice the vocabulary you've learned.

sentences.speaker: Beth
sentences.text: See you again soon, But for now, it's goodbye.

sentences.speaker: Neil
sentences.text: Goodbye.

sentences.speaker: Neil
sentences.text: Six Minute English

sentences.speaker: 片头片尾
